clue.text: Wet taking in a leftist

indicators.note: one word taking in another holds it inside, so the synonym for wet surrounds the letter

parts.note: wet means moist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A feeble moderate is absorbing a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' is British slang for a feeble moderate politician, which suits the leftist surface; here it is just the adjective meaning damp. 'taking in' puts A inside MOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A Maoist follows Chairman Mao's communism, so is a leftist.

clue.text: Marks I scaled differently for these examinations

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: differently means the letters are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: A teacher grades papers on a different scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' looks like exam grades but supplies M; 'differently' rearranges I SCALED into EDICALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicals are physical check-ups by a doctor.

clue.text: Wild asses, with good reason, ordered outside

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the single letter
ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Untamed donkeys sent out for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns REASON into ONAERS; 'outside' places it around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are a species of wild donkey from Asia.

clue.text: Single girl's best friend shows patience

explanation.surface: A lone woman's companion shows endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamonds are a girl's best friend', and a single set diamond is a solitaire; the card game for one player is called patience in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a lone gemstone in a ring; patience is the British name for the one-player card game.

clue.text: Decay in street is most alarming

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the dental word goes between the letters of the street abbreviation

parts.note: caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: Urban decay along a road is the most worrying sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decay' reads as urban rot in the street, but it is tooth decay. The definition includes 'is': the scariest thing is the most alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of scary, frightening to the highest degree.

clue.text: Nonconformist got Anglican or leader of Episcopalians converted

indicators.note: converted means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged
leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchgoer or bishop's follower changed denomination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' takes E from 'Episcopalians', and 'converted' rearranges it with GOT ANGLICAN OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Congregational churches are a Protestant denomination outside the Church of England, so dissenting.

clue.text: Gather outside clubs to do reviews

indicators.note: outside means the harvest word wraps the card suit letter

parts.note: to reap is to gather a crop
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer picks up clubs to write some critiques.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts REAP around C. 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or go over the main points again.

clue.text: Love I have of eating out

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone declares a passion for dining in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating out' looks like dining; it means wearing away, as water erodes rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosive describes something that wears away or corrodes.

clue.text: Gypsy fiddle

explanation.surface: A travelling musician plays a violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the violin; it is the verb to meddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker is an old word for a travelling person; to fiddle is to tinker with something.

clue.text: Reformed thief was closer, going straight

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former thief has come closer to honest living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going straight' suggests a reformed criminal; it means by the most direct route.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means by the shortest direct line between two places.

clue.text: Gluttony, perhaps, seen as lady dines out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman dining out is accused of overeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LADYDINES. Gluttony is one of the seven deadly sins, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven cardinal sins of Christian teaching.

clue.text: Cap person who represents country

explanation.surface: A sporting cap is given to someone who plays for their nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an international sports cap; instead a crown is a dental cap, and the Crown stands for the state in law.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist's cap for a tooth is a crown, and the monarch, or the Crown, embodies the nation in British law.

clue.text: Reported unfair player in this game

indicators.note: reported means the sound of the word is what counts, as if spoken

parts.note: someone who plays unfairly is a cheater

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be cheating at this game.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech CHEATER and CHEETAH sound alike. 'game' here means wild animals hunted, as in big game, not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game means large wild animals, and the big cat is among them.

clue.text: Anger about abuse of pet tortoise, say

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to anger is to rile

indicators.note: abuse of the word means it is mistreated and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Fury at the cruel treatment of a pet tortoise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse of' rearranges the pet word to EPT, and 'about' wraps the anger word round it. The tortoise is an example of the definition, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortoise is a shelled cold-blooded animal of that class.

clue.text: Maid appears with one cooling drink

parts.note: a maid is a young woman, a lass
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A serving girl comes in carrying something cold to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassi is an Indian yoghurt drink served chilled.

clue.text: See leader of gang in fraud sign an assumed name

indicators.note: the leading letter goes in the fraud word

parts.note: a con is a fraud or swindle

indicators.note: leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an omen is a sign

explanation.surface: Watch the gang boss sign a false name as part of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' takes G from 'gang', which 'in' places inside the fraud word. 'See' and 'an' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a nickname or added name, one taken on rather than given at birth.

clue.text: Outside broadcast term for thing getting out of control

parts.note: a term is a session, as in a school or court

explanation.surface: A remote television report on a period that has run wild.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is a preoccupation that takes over the mind.

clue.text: Tear round constantly showing respect

indicators.note: round means one word goes around the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
ever means constantly, always

explanation.surface: Racing about all the time while bowing to authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' looks like racing about; it is a rip. 'round' wraps the rip word around the always word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent means deeply respectful or devout.

clue.text: An important point simpleton endlessly gets wrong

indicators.note: gets wrong means the letters are put in a wrong order, rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A fool, as usual, misses an important point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final N of 'simpleton', leaving SIMPLETO, which 'gets wrong' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A milepost marks a significant stage or milestone, figuratively an important point.

clue.text: Crave traditional tales of evil spirits

indicators.note: lore of imps puts the spirit word first, before the tales word

parts.note: an imp is a small evil spirit, here used before another word
lore is traditional knowledge and tales

explanation.surface: Begging for old stories about demons.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave is an old sense of to beg, to plead earnestly.

clue.text: Dark place of exile's returned

indicators.note: returned means read back the other way

parts.note: Elba was Napoleon's place of exile, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A gloomy island prison has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was exiled to Elba; ELBA'S, with its S, read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is a poetic word for black, as in heraldry.

clue.text: Belong to dynasty with a cheerful countenance

parts.note: to belong to a group is to be a member, be a
the Ming were a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: Joining an imperial family, smiling widely.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BE A MING, the answer is belonging to the Ming dynasty of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beaming smiles broadly, showing happiness.

clue.text: Minister gives peers little time

parts.note: to peer is to pry, so peers means pries
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers lords a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peers' looks like lords; it is the verb, looks closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is a member of the clergy who ministers to a flock.

clue.text: Lecture to make an impression again

explanation.surface: A talk about printing again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as RE-PROOF: a proof is a printed impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke or telling-off; to re-proof is to take a fresh printer's proof.

clue.text: Apparent, if subtle, extra meaning one's missing

indicators.note: missing means the word is left out, removed from the other

parts.note: an overtone is an implied extra meaning
taken as written, the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A hint, however faint, can be obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes ONE from OVERTONE. 'if' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Person 'eld outside London finally acting

indicators.note: outside means this piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a person held captive is a hostage, here with the H dropped as in Cockney speech

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Cockney captive is detained outside London.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''eld' signals a dropped H in the answer piece too: 'OSTAGE. 'finally' takes N from 'London' and 'outside' puts 'OSTAGE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who is on-stage is performing in front of an audience.

clue.text: Call out 'yes' in woman's embrace

indicators.note: an embrace encloses, so the word for woman holds the other piece

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
OK means yes

explanation.surface: Shout assent while held by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embrace' puts the assent word inside the first woman of Genesis; 'in' only joins the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up or call forth a memory or feeling.

clue.text: Stress from electric current smashed silicate

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into pieces, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A shock of current shattered a mineral sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stress' reads as strain, but means emphasis in print. 'smashed' rearranges the mineral word into TALICISE, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting words in slanted type is a way to emphasise them.

clue.text: Iterates changes in composition

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: Repeating oneself alters a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges ITERATES.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written essay on a subject.

clue.text: Consider returning after taking good man on board

indicators.note: taking means swallowing up another letter inside
returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to consider is to think

explanation.surface: Have second thoughts after letting a decent fellow join the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns THINK to KNIHT; 'taking' puts G inside. 'man on board' looks like a crew member; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and this one moves in an L shape.
